what_it_does: Running AI image-recognition on a small battery-powered edge device (like a smart camera) is challenging because converting a raw camera image to digital form and then running a neural network consumes a lot of power. ResISC proposes doing the math in a fundamentally different number system called the Residue Number System (RNS), where instead of representing a number as a single large value, it is represented as a set of remainders after dividing by several small numbers — much like how telling someone 'it is 2 o'clock and also 2 days into the week' can uniquely identify a moment without a large calendar. RNS arithmetic avoids the carry chains that slow down conventional addition, enabling very fast and energy-efficient computation. The system converts the camera's analog signal directly into RNS digits before it even becomes digital pixels, then runs the neural network inference entirely in RNS using a memory technology called SOT-MRAM (a type of magnetic memory that can perform certain logic operations in place) to further save energy.
